staticComplianceReview.conclusion: Every FROM/JOIN target is a pg_catalog relation. Application relations (people, admin_users, etc.) are referenced only by name in catalog-join predicates (c.relname = 'people') to retrieve their structural metadata; no row of any application table is ever selected. Helper function definitions are retrieved via pg_get_functiondef; the functions themselves are never called.

findings.summary: Nested-object secret redactions did not propagate their _manual_review_required flag to the enclosing row, so flaggedSecretCandidateCount / noOutstandingSecretPatternMatches could under-report.
findings.reason: No column selected by VAM_OS_V5_METADATA_EVIDENCE_CAPTURE.sql is json/jsonb-typed today; only scalars and arrays, which were already handled correctly.
findings.verification: Three local dry runs (positive/negative/nested-secret) against fabricated non-secret stdin, no database or network access.

findings.component: execution wrapper (documented in decision pack, not a standalone tracked file)
findings.summary: STAGING_DATABASE_URL passed as a bare psql -d CLI argument is visible via host process listing for the life of the process.
findings.resolution: v2 pipeline removes -d entirely; STAGING_DATABASE_URL is exported as PGDATABASE (libpq env var, accepts a full connection URI) then immediately unset. No process argv created by the wrapper ever contains the value.
findings.residualRisk: Environment-variable exposure via same-privilege process-environment inspection is a materially smaller but non-zero surface than argv; accepted as documented, not eliminated to zero.

findings.summary: psql ... 2>&1 | node sanitizer can interleave/split lines under stdio buffering differences; verified this fails closed (spurious capture failure) rather than open (corrupted published evidence).
approvedStagingRefPresent / productionRefAbsent validate that template-carried ref strings survived cloning, not which server psql actually connected to at capture time.
findings.mitigation: Human must re-confirm STAGING_DATABASE_URL targets the approved ref immediately before the execution turn; this document's stagingTargetProof reflects a prior, not a current, check.
findings.resolution: v2 pipeline adds a non-printing target preflight (stagingVariablePresent/postgresUriShape/approvedStagingRefPresent/productionRefAbsent) that checks the live variable immediately before psql starts, and the sanitizer's session_context checks were strengthened (statementTimeoutBounded, lockTimeoutBounded, serverVersionPresent, databaseNamePresent). Target assurance is now explicitly two independent, non-substitutable parts: (A) pre-execution env-var preflight, (B) post-execution session-behavior evidence. Postgres has no self-referential project-ref signal, so no check can prove which project the open session belongs to; this residual is inherent to the technology.

round3StandaloneWrapper.scope: Moved the authoritative execution workflow out of the decision pack Markdown into one standalone, syntax-checked, hashable script file, and closed the remaining execution-safety gaps identified this round (hash-pinning of dependencies before any credential handling, checked/same-filesystem temp-directory creation, and signal-safe cleanup that cannot return a zero exit code on interruption). Local-only: no psql, no network, no STAGING_DATABASE_URL inspection or display (real or fabricated-as-real).
round3StandaloneWrapper.wrapperSha256Note: Recorded in the decision pack (Round-3 section) and the final report, not here -- the wrapper embeds this document's own hash as one of its hash-pinning constants, so this document is finalized and hashed BEFORE the wrapper is written, and is not edited again afterward to avoid a circular hash reference.

hashPinning.design: Before exporting PGDATABASE or invoking psql, the wrapper computes the actual SHA-256 of the sanitizer, the capture SQL, and this evidence document (acting as the sanitizer's template), and compares each against a literal expected-hash constant embedded in the wrapper's own source. Any mismatch fails closed before any credential is touched, printing only 'CAPTURE_FAILED reason=artifact_hash_mismatch artifact=<name>' where <name> is one of sanitizer/capture_sql/template_json -- never a hash value or file content.
hashPinning.purpose: Defends against the template, sanitizer, or capture SQL having been silently modified between this review and a future execution turn.

temporaryDirectoryDesign.previousDesign: OS temp directory via mktemp -d, with a documented but unverified same-filesystem assumption relative to the repository.
temporaryDirectoryDesign.currentDesign: A hidden, unpredictable-suffix directory created as a sibling of the repository root (under the repository's parent directory), so it is guaranteed outside the repository yet on the same filesystem/volume as the final evidence file by construction, not by assumption. mktemp -d's own exit status is checked; failure fails closed before any further state is created.
temporaryDirectoryDesign.prePublicationCheck: Immediately before the final atomic rename, the wrapper additionally compares the device ID (via `stat -c %d`) of the candidate's and the final destination's containing directories, and fails closed if they cannot be proven equal -- defense in depth on top of the by-construction guarantee, not a replacement for it. Not live-verified against this specific Windows/Git-Bash/NTFS environment in this database-free turn; flagged for a human spot-check with a non-secret dummy file before relying on it operationally.

signalSafety.design: Separate trap registrations for EXIT versus HUP/INT/TERM, using two distinct functions rather than one shared handler. The EXIT trap trusts $? (well-defined for EXIT traps). Each signal trap ignores $? entirely and exits with a hardcoded, signal-specific non-zero code (129/130/143 for HUP/INT/TERM), after disabling all traps (`trap - EXIT HUP INT TERM`) so the EXIT trap cannot re-fire and overwrite that code with whatever $? happened to be from the last command before the signal arrived.
signalSafety.reasoning: A single shared trap that does `local ec=$?; ...; exit "$ec"` for both EXIT and signals is unsafe: $? at signal-delivery time reflects the last completed command's status, not the signal, so an interruption immediately after a successful command could silently exit 0 -- indistinguishable from CAPTURE_OK to an unattended caller. This design makes that impossible by never trusting $? in the signal path.

round4CredentialScopeHardening.scope: Replaced the wrapper's global `export PGDATABASE="$STAGING_DATABASE_URL"` with a process-scoped assignment so the credential lives in the environment of the single psql child process only, never in the wrapper's own persistent shell environment. Local-only: no psql, no network, no STAGING_DATABASE_URL inspection or display (real or fabricated-as-real).

design.startupUnsets: PGDATABASE, PGHOST, PGHOSTADDR, PGPORT, PGUSER, PGPASSWORD, PGPASSFILE, PGSERVICE, PGSERVICEFILE, PGOPTIONS are all unset at wrapper startup, before PGSSLMODE/PGCONNECT_TIMEOUT are set, so no inherited libpq variable from a parent process can combine with or override the URI handled later.
design.credentialHolder: DB_URI (a plain, never-exported shell variable) replaces the prior design's exported PGDATABASE as the temporary holder for STAGING_DATABASE_URL's value, set only after the non-printing preflight has already passed.
design.psqlInvocation: PGDATABASE="$DB_URI" "$PSQL" -X -q -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -f "$SQLFILE" -- a simple-command prefix assignment, which bash scopes to that one child process's environment only and never adds to argv or to the wrapper's own exported environment.
design.sanitizerInvocation: piped through `env -u PGDATABASE -u DB_URI -u STAGING_DATABASE_URL -u PGPASSWORD node "$SANITIZER" ...` -- explicit, self-documenting proof in the wrapper's own source that the sanitizer process cannot inherit any of the four credential-bearing variable names, even though none of them were ever exported to begin with.
design.postPipelineCleanup: DB_URI is unset immediately after PIPE_CODES=("${PIPESTATUS[@]}") is captured, and again defensively (along with STAGING_DATABASE_URL, PGDATABASE, PGPASSWORD) inside remove_temp_state(), which both the EXIT and every signal handler call.
